parts.text:
6
An aircraft on a runway accelerates uniformly from rest to its take-off speed of 58 m s–1.
The acceleration of the aircraft is 4.2 m s–2, and the aircraft uses 74% of the length of the runway
to reach its take-off speed.
What is the length of the runway?
A
300 m
B
540 m
C
590 m
D
800 m

hints: Notice the aircraft starts from rest, so $u = 0$, with $v = 58 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $a = 4.2 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ for the motion up to take-off.
Connect these to the equation without time, $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, to first find the distance travelled to reach take-off speed.
Remember that calculated distance is only 74% of the runway, so divide it by $0.74$ to find the full runway length.
walkthrough: List the motion to take-off: initial velocity $u = 0$, final velocity $v = 58 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and uniform acceleration $a = 4.2 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ because time is not given or asked for. With $u = 0$ this rearranges to $s = v^2/(2a)$.
Substitute with units: $s = (58 \text{ m s}^{-1})^2 / (2 \times 4.2 \text{ m s}^{-2}) = 3364 / 8.4 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the take-off distance: $s \approx 400.5 \text{ m}$. This uses only 74% of the runway.
Find the full length $L$ from $0.74 \times L = s$, so $L = s / 0.74 \approx 400.5 / 0.74 \text{ m} \approx 541 \text{ m}$.
Rounded to two significant figures this is $540 \text{ m}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is about $300 \text{ m}$, found by multiplying the take-off distance by $0.74$ instead of dividing by it.

B.explanation: This matches the take-off distance of about $400 \text{ m}$ divided by $0.74$ to give the full runway length.

C.explanation: This is too large and does not follow from $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $v = 58 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $a = 4.2 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

D.explanation: This is about $800 \text{ m}$, found by omitting the factor $2$ in $v^2 = 2as$ to get $58^2/4.2$.
